records.content: Dhruv Dave (goes by DKD). AI Engineer with a data engineering background. Currently pursuing an MBA in Business Analytics (in collaboration with KPMG) but actively targeting technical AI/ML engineering roles, not management or pure business-analyst roles.

AI Engineer with a data engineering background and 3+ years building data and GenAI systems on Azure and Databricks. Works hands-on with RAG, multi-agent systems (LangGraph), vector search, and ETL/lakehouse pipelines. Strong at turning unclear business problems into working systems that are traceable and auditable.

Designed and built a working client POC — an enterprise Context Layer on Azure Databricks — to fix a core failure mode in a Pharma engagement: AI agents run directly against Unity Catalog data returned unreliable, ungoverned answers because they lacked the client's ontology, canonical metric definitions, and business logic (in one case inferring pharmacovigilance safety signals, an unacceptable risk in regulated Pharma).
highlights: Engineered a multi-agent system with a LangGraph supervisor that classifies user intent (keyword + foundation-model LLM) and dynamically routes each query to one of two strictly isolated, governed paths (never blended), preserving auditability and correctness.
Implemented a governed Analytics path (Databricks Genie over certified Unity Catalog metric views, using on-behalf-of user identity so column masks and row-level access are enforced per user).
Implemented a governed Knowledge path (hybrid keyword + semantic vector retrieval over documents in UC Volumes via service-principal identity).

Embedded governance into every response (route provenance, source citations, audit metadata), backed by write-only Delta audit logs and a pharmacovigilance human-approval trace, surfaced through a React + Vite Databricks App with a FastAPI auth and domain-routing layer.

records.name: Operational Context Engine (OCE)
records.status: Advanced to Phase 2, top 12%; results pending (Aug 2026).
records.content: An AI-native context layer for industrial operations. Problem: operations teams stay in reactive firefighting because operational data is fragmented across historians, MES, ERP, and maintenance logs, and tribal knowledge is lost between shifts. Approach: map operational data to a shared ontology and canonical definitions, then apply RAG + LLM reasoning over a governed knowledge substrate to deliver evidence-cited, proactive root-cause analysis instead of raw alerts. Outcome: a reference design that shifts operations from reactive to proactive, extending the governed context-layer thinking from the KPMG work into the industrial/manufacturing domain.

AI / LLMs: foundation-model integration (OpenAI, Anthropic, Hugging Face, Ollama)
Data & AI Platforms: Azure (Data Lake Storage, Data Factory, Blob Storage, Synapse, Functions)
